title: Agent Interoperability Protocols (A2A / ACP)
abstract: The Agent2Agent (A2A) protocol and its predecessor ACP (Agent Communication Protocol) define how AI agents discover, communicate, and collaborate with each other — complementing MCP which handles agent-to-tool communication.
why_we_care: As multi-agent systems become standard architecture for GenAI applications, a standard protocol for agent-to-agent communication is critical. Without it, every agent integration is bespoke. A2A is emerging as the Linux Foundation-backed standard with support from Google, IBM, Microsoft, AWS, Cisco, Salesforce, ServiceNow, and SAP. Understanding it now positions us to build interoperable agent systems rather than locked-in ones.
summary: A2A (Agent2Agent Protocol) is an open standard for agent-to-agent communication, now at v1.0 under the Linux Foundation. It originated from Google (April 2025) while ACP (Agent Communication Protocol) was created independently by IBM/BeeAI (March 2025). In August 2025, ACP merged into A2A, consolidating the ecosystem into a single standard. A2A uses JSON-RPC 2.0 over HTTP(S), supports Agent Cards for discovery, and enables synchronous, streaming, and asynchronous interactions. It is complementary to MCP: MCP connects agents to tools, A2A connects agents to agents.
description:
**What is A2A?**

The Agent2Agent (A2A) protocol is an open standard enabling AI agents built on different frameworks, by different teams, running on separate servers to communicate and collaborate as peers — not just as tools. It reached v1.0 in March 2026 under the Linux Foundation.

**Key Capabilities**
- **Agent Discovery**: Via "Agent Cards" detailing capabilities and connection info
- **Standardized Communication**: JSON-RPC 2.0 over HTTP(S)
- **Flexible Interaction**: Synchronous request/response, streaming (SSE), and async push notifications
- **Rich Data Exchange**: Text, files, structured JSON
- **Opacity**: Agents collaborate without exposing internal memory, logic, or tool implementations

**What was ACP?**

The Agent Communication Protocol (ACP) was created by IBM Research to power the BeeAI platform. It used a REST-based approach with OpenAPI specification. Key concepts included Agent Manifests, Runs, Messages/MessageParts, Await (interactive exchanges), and Sessions. ACP was donated to the Linux Foundation in March 2025 and officially merged into A2A in August 2025 — the ACP repository is now archived.

**A2A vs MCP — Complementary Standards**
- **MCP** (Model Context Protocol): Connects an AI agent to tools, data sources, and resources. Think of it as how an agent uses tools.
- **A2A**: Connects AI agents to other AI agents. Think of it as how agents talk to each other.
- Together they form the emerging standard stack: MCP for tool access, A2A for agent collaboration.

**Ecosystem & Governance**
- Linux Foundation project with TSC members from Google, IBM, Microsoft, AWS, Cisco, Salesforce, ServiceNow, SAP
- SDKs: Python, Go, JavaScript, Java, .NET
- 22.5k GitHub stars, 145+ contributors
- DeepLearning.AI short course available

**Why This Matters for GEE**

As we build and evaluate GenAI tools (Copilot, Claude Code, Kiro, Strands), the next frontier is making these agents work together. A2A defines how a code review agent could delegate to a security scanning agent, or how an orchestrator could coordinate specialized agents across teams. Understanding A2A now informs our architecture decisions for multi-agent systems.
